p: Here is, 1. A good caution against presuming upon time to come: Boast not thyself, no, not of to-morrow, much less of many days or years to come. …
Solomon here, as often in this book, shows that the poor have in some respects the advantage of the rich; for, 1. They have a better relish of their enjoyments than the rich have. …
This we had before, ch. xxii. 3. Note, 1. Evil may be foreseen. …

This intimates both the pleasure and the advantage of conversation. This is designed to encourage diligence, faithfulness, and constancy, even in mean employments. This shows us that there is a way, 1. Of knowing ourselves. …
This gives us a touchstone by which we may try ourselves. …
